verdict.rationale: Penpot provides building blocks for background automation: outbound webhooks fire on events such as file creation or updates and comments, access tokens let apps call its API, and its MCP server and plugin API are marketed for workflow automation and automating tedious tasks. The autonomous, always-running part, however, must be built and hosted externally (webhook receivers, agents, scripts) rather than configured inside Penpot. Missing for 10: a native automation or scheduling feature, documented autonomous agent or background-run modes, and hands-on evidence of unattended automations working.
